title: Tyres, Wheels & Wheel Nuts
whatItIs: Check tyres and wheel fixings every day. Large vehicles need at least 1 mm of tread, the right pressures, no deep cuts or visible cord, and tight wheel nuts.

keyFacts.text: Large vehicles MUST have at least 1 mm of tread across 3/4 of the breadth, in a continuous band all the way round.
Tyres MUST be inflated to the manufacturer's specification for the load being carried.
Tyres over 10 years old MUST NOT be used on the front axles of goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes.
The tyre's date of manufacture marking MUST always be legible.

keyFacts: Check wheel nuts are tight: wheel nut indicators, if fitted, show whether nuts have moved.

onTheTest.question: What's the minimum legal tread depth for a lorry tyre?
onTheTest.why: Large vehicles must have at least 1 mm of tread across three-quarters of the breadth and in a continuous band all the way round.

onTheTest.question: Which tyre finding on your walkaround check is a defect?
options: Wheel nut indicators all lined up
Pressures matching the handbook for the load
onTheTest.why: Check there's no cord visible anywhere on the tyre and no deep cuts in the sidewall. Visible cord is a defect to report.

traps: 1.6 mm is the limit for cars and light vans. For lorries it's 1 mm.
Check pressures when tyres are cold: warm tyres can give a misleading reading.
Look between twin wheels: no objects or debris should be trapped there.
